prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules direct E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glues.

statement.case_for: I keep B037 as a single prize part with Crews, Deshaies and Handa; my preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1. After reading all eight statements, the scientific case still rests on one idea that can be tested rather than only counted: a small molecule that induces proximity between a target and an E3 ligase makes the cell remove the protein catalytically. That is a genuinely new way for a molecule to act, it has been reproduced by many independent laboratories for more than two decades, and the cereblon finding resolved the long-standing question of how thalidomide acts. From my own field I can add that ubiquitin-dependent turnover of proteins such as the RNR small subunit is a normal regulatory layer for nucleotide pools, so the premise that the proteasome pathway can be redirected by chemistry is biologically well grounded. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated heterobifunctional degradation, and Handa's identification of cereblon is the mechanistic discovery on which the glue strand stands, so the trio covers both strands at their points of origin.
statement.case_against: Attribution and maturity remain the real costs. Eight people are credited and any trio omits Sakamoto, who co-invented the first PROTAC, Ciulli, who gave the field VHL ligands and the ternary-complex cooperativity framework, and Gray, Ito and Kim. The PROTAC and glue strands also have different histories, because lenalidomide was effective before its mechanism was known. No PROTAC is yet approved, so the clinical vindication that normally accompanies a prize of this kind is incomplete and the committee could be a few years early. If the committee judges that early, or judges the credit unrecoverable, B005 is the fallback I would accept, and B060 stays my second alternative, with its own CRISPR-boundary and Nishida-Kondo questions.

responses.point: B005 is a general, mechanistically understood transformation with about 25 years of independent confirmation and industrial use, so recognition is overdue rather than premature, whereas B037 depends on clinical outcomes still to come and B005 has the cleaner two-person credit.
responses.response: I agree that B005 is the better case on attribution and has no maturity risk, and that is why it is an alternative of mine. Where I differ is on what the maturity test should measure. For B037 the scientific claim, that E3 recruitment produces catalytic loss of a target, is settled by two decades of independent work, and thalidomide-class glues already have an established clinical record, so clinical outcomes of bifunctional degraders affect the size of the impact rather than whether it is real. Your own stated objection to B005, overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize, also seems to me the more serious conceptual limit: the C-N work is a distinct ligand-design achievement, but it extends a recognised modality, whereas B037 opens a new one. I would move to B005 if the committee decides that an unapproved bifunctional degrader is disqualifying.

responses.point: B037 is a design strand plus a mechanistic strand with different histories, because lenalidomide worked clinically before its mechanism was known, and B005 is the safer choice if the committee judges the timing early.
responses.response: I accept that the two strands have different histories, and I think the citation should say so rather than hide it, which is why I name the cereblon identification explicitly as the mechanistic discovery and not as a design step. I do not think the serendipitous origin of the glues weakens the prize: the credit is for showing how E3 recruitment explains a drug that already worked, and then for the lesson that this can be designed. On your fallback, I share it in substance, but I would apply it only if the committee concludes that the absence of an approved PROTAC is a true maturity gap, which I do not believe it is, given reproducibility and the glue clinical record. Regulatory approval of a bifunctional degrader before the vote would simply remove the objection.

responses.point: The attribution question for B037 could be handled by replacing Deshaies with or adding Ciulli (Crews, Handa, Ciulli), crediting structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity, and a two-part chemical-biology configuration (B002 plus B060) could better reflect chemistry.
responses.response: I considered the Crews, Handa and Ciulli trio seriously. Ciulli's VHL ligands and cooperativity work are a real chemical contribution and the committee will have to defend leaving him out. I still keep Deshaies because the first heterobifunctional degrader, the 2001 PROTAC, was a joint Crews-Deshaies-Sakamoto idea, and a PROTAC citation without both of its conceptual originators is harder to defend than one without the later optimisation work. On the B060 half of your configuration, I changed my own ranking away from it for the same reasons you list, the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Nishida and Kondo parallel report, and I find that a Liu-alone credit is less secure than I argued in the opening. I do not find the two-part B002 plus B060 configuration more convincing than a single strong part, since neither part has the breadth of support that B037 has.

responses.point: The chair asks whether PROTACs and glues should be one part or two, and whether the three-name cap forces an attribution that looks assembled.
responses.response: My answer is one part, and I have left the two-part fallback I floated in round 1 aside after the round: splitting would need names for each half and the three-name cap makes that unnatural, giving only one or two names per strand. A single citation that states the shared principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, with the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism as the two supporting results, is more honest than a split. I agree with your own caution that opening support is not merit, and my confidence in B037 comes from the independent reproduction and the thalidomide mechanism, not from the count of first places.

uncertainties: Whether leaving out Sakamoto and Ciulli can be defended in a public citation, and whether the committee should prefer the cleaner credit of B005 for that reason.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC is a real maturity problem or a clinical lag, and whether a first approval would change the committee's view.
Whether PROTACs and glues are one coherent achievement or two, and whether one citation can carry both without looking assembled.
Whether base editing (B060) is sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and how to treat Nishida and Kondo.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has changed since round 1. My research on nucleotide metabolism and genome stability overlaps in topic with base editing (B060) and DNA-repair condensates (B024), and ubiquitin-dependent turnover of RNR is adjacent to B037, but I have no recorded personal, collaborative or institutional tie to any credited person on the shortlist and propose no recusal.
